newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities were steady to higher in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Monday.

"The interbank rate eased slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.65/1.60 percent compared with last Thursday's yield of 1.63/1.58 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.72/1.67 percent against 1.70/1.65 percent.
Among bonds, April 1998 was unchanged from last Thursday's close of S$99.53/99.58.
September 2001 ended at S$96.69/96.74 against Thursday's close of S$96.67/96.72 and June 2003 at S$94.73/94.78 from S$94.72/94.77.
The interbank rate eased to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent versus last Thursday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
